DEFINE.core_strategy: Report the byte size of the input in the success line beside the character count. Measure it from the raw input as read, once, the same way for a file and for standard input. Keep every other count, error and invocation unchanged.

rejected_alternatives.direction: Derive the byte count from the decoded text by turning it back into bytes
rejected_alternatives.tradeoff: It measures the decoded text, not the raw input. The count could drift from the true input size if decoding ever changes.

rejected_alternatives.direction: Read the byte size from the file system's own record of file size
rejected_alternatives.tradeoff: Standard input has no such record, so file and '-' would take different paths. Parity between them would break.

rejected_alternatives.direction: Offer the byte count only behind a new opt-in command-line flag
rejected_alternatives.tradeoff: The user wants it shown next to characters by default. A new flag also breaks the guardrail of no new arguments.

rejected_alternatives.direction: Document that users should run a separate byte-counting tool
rejected_alternatives.tradeoff: It leaves the core problem unsolved. Users still need a second tool to size buffers, uploads or storage.

dependencies.description: The approved shared read and decode path for file and standard input from SPEC-0004
An architecture update that moves bytes from the hello system's 'Does NOT own' list into what it owns
The four Quality Gate commands recorded in AGENTS.md

assumptions.description: 'Next to the characters count' means the byte field sits right after the character field and before the line field.
assumptions.validator: The user who asked for the byte count
assumptions.how_checked: Confirm the field order during strategy review, before SPEC fixes the exact output line
assumptions.if_false: Move the field to the position the user names. The strategy direction does not change.

assumptions.description: Users expect invalid UTF-8 input to keep failing with the existing error, with no byte count printed.
assumptions.validator: The user who asked for the byte count
assumptions.how_checked: Confirm during strategy review that the error behavior stays unchanged
assumptions.if_false: Re-open DEFINE on whether undecodable input should report bytes only.

assumptions.description: The raw bytes a file holds equal the bytes the same content sends on standard input.
assumptions.validator: The existing file-and-stdin parity tests from SPEC-0004, extended with the byte field
assumptions.how_checked: Feed each SPEC-0004 byte sample through a file and through '-' and compare the full output lines
assumptions.if_false: Re-open DISCOVER on what differs between the two sources.

risks.description: Adding a fourth field changes the success line again and breaks scripts that parse the three-field form
risks.impact: Users' scripts could misread counts after upgrading
risks.mitigation: Document the new line in README.md and state that the three-field form no longer applies

risks.description: Existing tests assert the three-field line and must be updated
risks.impact: The Quality Gate fails until those tests change, and an edit could weaken a guardrail
risks.mitigation: Limit test edits to the expected success line and keep every other assertion unchanged

risks.description: The byte count could be taken from a second read of the input
risks.impact: Standard input cannot be read twice, so the '-' path could report a wrong count
risks.mitigation: Require one read per run, shared by the byte count and the decode

DEFINE.thesis: Show the raw byte size of the input beside the character count, so users stop needing a second tool, now that file and stdin share one path.

goals.description: Users learn the byte size of their input from the same wordcount run that gives the other counts
goals.why: Users who size buffers, uploads or storage now need a second tool
goals.success_metric: 100% of successful runs print a byte field equal to the raw input size

goals.description: The byte count is identical for a file and for standard input through '-' with the same bytes
goals.why: DG-0005 requires parity, and the existing output is already identical across both sources
goals.success_metric: All SPEC-0004 byte samples give identical four-field lines for file and '-'

success_criteria.criterion: Byte count matches raw input size for non-ASCII text
success_criteria.measurement: Automated test on 'café' encoded as UTF-8

success_criteria.criterion: File and standard input parity including bytes
success_criteria.measurement: Parity tests over the SPEC-0004 byte samples
success_criteria.baseline: 100% identical three-field lines, no byte field

success_criteria.criterion: Existing counts, errors and invocation unchanged
success_criteria.measurement: Existing guardrail tests from SPEC-0001 to SPEC-0004
success_criteria.target: All pass, with only the expected success line updated

non_goals.description: Reporting a byte count for input that is not valid UTF-8
non_goals.tradeoff: Keeps the existing single-line error and empty stdout. Users with undecodable input still need another tool.

non_goals.description: Other statistics such as longest line or per-line output
non_goals.tradeoff: Keeps the change small and focused on the approved byte-size problem.

non_goals.description: Totals or several inputs in one invocation
non_goals.tradeoff: Keeps the single-input contract. Users who need totals must sum runs themselves.
The user declined them. Review relies on the walkthrough and README instead.

in_scope: A byte field in the success line, placed beside the character field
Byte count measured from the raw input, read once, for files and for '-'
README.md documents the new output line, the byte rule, and that the three-field form no longer applies
Updating existing tests only where they assert the success line
out_of_scope: Changes to the word, character or line rules (existing, unchanged)
The '-' standard input invocation itself (existing, from SPEC-0004)
Byte counts for invalid UTF-8 input
Non-UTF-8 encodings, totals or several inputs

walkthrough.name: Sizing a non-ASCII file
today: The user runs wordcount on a file holding 'café'.
The output shows words: 1 characters: 4 lines: 0.
The user runs a second tool to learn the file is 5 bytes.
with_strategy: The user runs wordcount on the same file.
The output shows the 5-byte size beside the 4 characters, with words and lines unchanged.
The user needs no second tool.

walkthrough.name: Piping the same bytes through standard input
today: The output matches the file run but gives no byte size.
with_strategy: The user pipes the same bytes into wordcount -.
The output shows 6 bytes, and the line is identical to the file run.

walkthrough.name: Undecodable input
today: The user passes a file with bytes that are not valid UTF-8.
wordcount prints one error line and exits with status 1.
with_strategy: The same run prints the same error line and exits with status 1.
